Vehicle assumptions

Stages burn sequentially. Dry mass may be jettisoned after each burn. Capability uses the ideal rocket equation multiplied by the entered burn efficiency. Launch-vehicle ascent from a planetary surface is not modeled.

Operations products

Generates an operations-readiness estimate, communications and power budgets, covariance growth, correction reserve, flyby B-plane indicators and a command timeline. This is a planning layer, not flight certification.

Planet texture manager

Choose JPG, PNG or WEBP files. File names may include a planet name, moon, probe, spacecraft, stars, or milky.
Embedded planet and background textures are active.

Validation mission presets

Presets reproduce public milestone dates for geometry comparison; they do not claim to reconstruct each mission’s complete operational trajectory.

Live data interfaces

JPL Horizons vectorsJPL SBDB objectsAnalytical fallback

Live data requires internet access and browser permission for NASA/JPL API requests. The simulation automatically falls back to embedded orbital elements when a request fails. Venus and Mercury maps are embedded from the Solar System Scope CC BY 4.0 texture set, based on NASA imagery and elevation data.

Accuracy boundary

This browser suite now covers preliminary targeting, trade studies and educational engineering analysis. Operational navigation still requires validated kernels, mission-specific force models, covariance, tracking data and independent verification.
